papers.title: L Antigen Family Member 3 stabilizes stalled replication forks by reducing MRE11 resection to maintain genome stability.
papers.summary: LAGE3, a KEOPS complex core component, protects stalled replication forks from degradation under replication stress. Turboid proximity labeling identified MRE11 as an interacting nuclease; LAGE3 deficiency causes unscheduled fork resection in an MRE11-dependent manner. GAMOS-associated LAGE3 mutations disrupt KEOPS assembly and fork recruitment, driving genome instability. Establishes LAGE3 as a stalled-fork protector and links KEOPS to GAMOS pathogenesis.

papers.title: A single-cell transcriptome atlas reveals paradoxical monoallelic expression of RNA editing and heterozygous SNPs.
papers.summary: Analyzing 13,025 Drosophila single-cell Smart-seq libraries, the authors found 94% of A-to-I RNA editing sites and 92.8% of heterozygous SNPs show binary (0/1) allelic expression per cell. They caution this binary pattern—from monoallelic transcriptional bursts, dropout, or amplification bias—means Smart-seq may poorly capture molecular diversity, and single-cell results should be interpreted conservatively.

papers.title: Assembly of exon junction complexes on spliceosomes begins before spliceosome activation.
papers.summary: Using immunoprecipitation with RNase I plus LC-MS/MS in HEK293T cells, the authors mapped when exon junction complex (EJC) components assemble on spliceosomes. They report eIF4A3, RBM8A, MAGOH, and the RNPS1-EJC associate with assembled but inactive spliceosomes, while CASC3 joins late activated spliceosomes. This fills long-standing gaps in the ordering of EJC assembly during pre-mRNA splicing.

papers.title: Limits of deep-learning-based RNA prediction methods.
papers.summary: Benchmarking 10 deep-learning RNA prediction methods on an independent, non-redundant dataset, AlphaFold3 and Boltz-1 performed best for monomeric RNA, but accuracy depended on similarity to training data; structurally divergent RNAs stayed poorly modeled. For RNA complexes the two leading methods strongly outperformed HelixFold3 and RoseTTAFoldNA. The authors conclude current methods recognize recurring motifs rather than generalizing to novel RNA folds.

papers.title: hY3 RNA binds and inhibits ribosomes and modulates the starvation-induced integrated stress response.
papers.summary: The human Y3 (hY3) RNA is identified as a ribosome-associated non-coding RNA that inhibits protein synthesis and attenuates metabolism, especially during starvation. Depleting hY3 reduces eIF2a phosphorylation, blunts the integrated stress response, and disrupts the survival/apoptosis balance. hY3 emerges as a ribosome-bound determinant of cell fate under metabolic stress.

papers.title: Massively parallel characterization of RNA G-quadruplex stability and molecular recognition.
papers.summary: Using reverse-transcriptase stop sequencing across ~3,000 synthetic RNA G-quadruplexes (rG4s), the authors quantified sequence features driving rG4 stability—g-tract length, loops, and flanking sequences. The pyridostatin ligand preferentially stabilized rG4s with mixed-length g-tracts, and protein-binding assays revealed features recognized by G3BP1 and FMRP. Provides a generalizable framework for rG4 stability, RBP recognition, and ligand interactions.

papers.title: MFDB: a comprehensive database for marine fish functional genomics and evolutionary genomics.
papers.summary: MFDB (marinefishdb.cn) is presented as the first integrative genomics platform for marine teleosts, compiling multi-omics resources across 89 species including genome assemblies, phylogenomics, collinearity, pan-gene sets, gene architectures, annotations, expression profiles, and gene-family analyses. It offers tissue-specific co-expression networks, lineage-defining gene repertoires, and macrosynteny models, plus an intuitive programmable interface for cross-omics mining and molecular breeding.

papers.title: Zinc increases stress granule formation by promoting RNA condensation.
papers.summary: The authors show cells modulate intracellular zinc, which directly promotes RNA condensation and stress granule formation. Oxidative stress raises labile zinc and metallothionein expression; increased zinc boosts stress granule formation and delays disassembly at ~100x lower concentrations than magnesium, while zinc depletion reduces granules. Zinc emerges as an unappreciated regulator of RNA structure and stress granule biology.

papers.title: Hepatocellular carcinoma organoids enable drug discovery and combination therapy across heterogeneous tumors.
papers.summary: From a biobank of patient-derived hepatocellular carcinoma organoids generated across disease stages, high-throughput screening of >1,600 compounds identified multiple active agents including drug-repurposing candidates. Rationally designed doublet and triplet combinations anchored on regorafenib improved efficacy across heterogeneous tumors with selectivity over non-tumoral cells; a selected triplet showed improved in vivo tumor control and tolerability.

papers.title: The R-loop-SPT6-SETD2 axis safeguards H3K36me3 to prevent broad H3K4me3 invasion in mouse oocytes.
papers.summary: In mouse oocytes the R-loop-SPT6-SETD2 axis safeguards H3K36me3 to prevent broad H3K4me3 invasion. R-loops stabilize SETD2 via SPT6; losing r-loops reduces H3K36me3 in oocyte-specific gene bodies, triggering H3K4me3 invasion and gene repression. dCas9-mediated SETD2 restoration rescued local expression, and SUPT6 overexpression corrected the imbalance and alleviated meiotic arrest, establishing R-loops as critical regulators of maternal chromatin.

papers.title: A single-cell transcriptomic atlas reveals the immune panorama of neonatal sepsis.
papers.summary: Single-cell RNA-seq of 26 blood samples from 18 neonates across acute sepsis, convalescence, and healthy controls identified 57 cell subtypes. Sepsis featured lymphoid depletion with myeloid expansion; S100A8+ MDSC-like cells drove a cytokine storm via an S100-TLR4-MYD88 feedforward loop, coexisting with multi-lineage immunoparalysis (CD4 mitochondrial dysfunction, hyper-suppressive Tregs, exhausted CD8 T cells). Nominates the S100-TLR4 axis and mitochondrial dysregulation as therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Arrhythmic zone: When circadian clocks go quiet in the cold.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence that circadian clocks can weaken or disappear at cold temperatures still within an organism's survival range—the 'arrhythmic zone' bounded by the lower critical temperature for rhythmicity and minimum viability. Examples span cyanobacteria (Hopf bifurcation ~19 C), Arabidopsis (damped at 4 C), and hibernating mammalian SCN (arrested below ~15-17 C). Candidate mechanisms, adaptive significance, and the gap in psychrophile data are examined.

papers.title: Distinct regulation of Wnt signaling and EPZ5676 governs human UiPSM reprogramming via the CDX2/T/TBX6 core axis.
papers.summary: Using integrated multi-omic and functional analyses of induced presomitic mesoderm (UiPSM), the authors show Wnt/beta-catenin activation by CHIR is essential for reprogramming, while EPZ5676 controls timing and efficiency. CDX2, T (brachyury), and TBX6 form a partially redundant core axis; CDX2 maintains chromatin accessibility of Wnt3a/T/TBX6 in a positive feedback loop. A stable network preserves UiPSM identity and stemness, clarifying human mesoderm specification.

papers.title: Integrated in silico and in vivo approaches reveal naltrexone as a synergistic modulator of TLR4 and μ-opioid receptors restoring redox homeostasis via Nrf2/Keap-1/HO-1 and HIF-1α/VEGF pathways in COPD.
papers.summary: Ultra-low-dose naltrexone was evaluated against cigarette-smoke-induced COPD in vivo. Naltrexone (selected over naloxone by ADMET/docking) attenuated airway inflammation and emphysema, restored redox homeostasis via Nrf2/Keap-1/HO-1 and HIF-1a/VEGF pathways, and reduced apoptosis markers (cleaved caspase-3, carbonyls, lipid peroxidation) while downregulating TLR4 and mu-opioid receptor expression, supporting dual-target modulation of key immunoinflammatory pathways.

papers.title: Inhibiting endoplasmic reticulum stress and unfolded protein response: an effective strategy for chemoprevention of hepatocarcinogenesis.
papers.summary: In a DEN-induced rat hepatocarcinogenesis model, the endoplasmic-reticulum chaperone-inducer BIX was tested for chemoprevention. BIX impeded tumor growth, lowered histological grade, and reduced UPR gene/protein expression (PERK, ATF-6, CHOP, p-PERK/PERK). Decreased inflammatory and proliferative markers with increased apoptosis markers confirmed BIX attenuates ER-stress-driven UPR activation and suppresses hepatocarcinogenesis.

papers.title: Accelerated organelle movements can indirectly affect the motility of other organelles in plant cells.
papers.summary: Using 'booster' and 'anchor' constructs, the authors manipulated organelle movements in Nicotiana benthamiana leaf epidermal cells. Mitochondrial boosters increased motility of all tested organelles and reorganized actin; ER boosters selectively enhanced Golgi and peroxisome movement, suggesting specific organelle interactions. Anchoring to microtubules reduced targeted-organelle motility without consistent effects on others. Organelle movement can occur independently yet is coordinated across types.

papers.title: Potential role of myeloid bodies in protection against photo-oxidative damage of the retinal pigment epithelium.
papers.summary: In the sablefish retina, unusually large myeloid bodies (organized smooth ER) containing cisternae perpendicular to Bruch's membrane were found to exclusively bind short-wavelength (blue) light-absorbing opsins and a zeaxanthin-linked enzyme. Because blue light strongly drives photo-oxidation, sequestration within myeloid bodies suggests the smooth ER plays an optical filtering role protecting the retinal pigment epithelium from photo-oxidative damage.

papers.title: Identification and Classification of Expressed Orphan Genes, Spurious Orphan Genes, and Conserved Genes in the Human Gut Microbiome.
papers.summary: Combining ~5,000 human gut microbiome metatranscriptome libraries with machine learning, ~218,000 orphan genes were found expressed while ~330,000 were classified spurious (no detectable expression). XGBoost classifiers distinguished expressed orphans (AUC 0.82) and conserved genes (AUC 0.93), with SHAP showing expressed orphans are shorter and present in more genomes. Expressed orphan genes differ systematically from conserved and spurious ones in composition and evolutionary signals.

papers.title: Moulting in Pancrustacea is characterised by both deeply conserved and recently evolved gene modules.
papers.summary: Public transcriptomic datasets across five pancrustacean species revealed moulting gene expression comprises both deeply conserved and lineage-specific modules. Lineage-specific signatures are not uniform across moulting: the middle transitional phase is more lineage-specific, showing an inverse hourglass pattern, likely reflecting cuticle development and life-history-specific exoskeleton structures. Supports both evolutionary conservation and divergence in the modular moulting program.

papers.title: Clinical outcomes of 1PN- and 3PN-derived blastocysts in the absence of transferable 2PN embryos: A retrospective analysis.
papers.summary: A retrospective analysis of 150 patients examined embryos derived from 1PN and 3PN zygotes in the absence of transferable 2PN embryos. 1PN zygotes had significantly lower blastocyst formation than both 2PN and 3PN. All PGT-A-tested blastocysts were aneuploid and none transferred. Among transfers performed without genetic testing, the only pregnancy occurred after combined 1PN and 3PN blastocyst transfer.

papers.title: Role of connexin 43 in hyperoxia-induced bronchopulmonary dysplasia and associated pulmonary hypertension.
papers.summary: This study tested the connexin 43 gap-junction inhibitor 43Gap26 in a hyperoxia-induced bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) rat model and human fetal pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells. While 43Gap26 reduced hyperoxia-induced Cx43 overexpression and partially improved alveolarization, it failed to prevent lung-function alterations, surfactant deficits, ECM remodeling, macrophage M2 polarization, TIMP-1 secretion, pulmonary hypertension, or mortality—indicating only partial protective efficacy.

papers.title: Cryopreservation of aldehyde-fixed whole brains.
papers.summary: A protocol for aldehyde-based cryopreservation (ABC) preserves fixed whole brains via graded immersion cryoprotection (50% ethylene glycol, 30% sucrose in fixative) and subzero storage. CT tracking showed ~9 months required for cryoprotectant equilibration throughout whole human brains; insufficient diffusion caused ice-crystal artifacts, while refined equilibration preserved cellular architecture and ultrastructure. Provides a method for long-term subzero storage of fixed whole brains.

papers.title: An integrated systems biology and machine learning framework for identifying potential biomarkers and pathways in autism spectrum disorder.
papers.summary: Integrating GEO peripheral blood expression (GSE18123), WGCNA, PPI networks, and machine-learning feature selection (LASSO, random forest), the authors prioritized TLR8 and CASP4 plus miRNAs (miR-891b, miR-627-3p for TLR8; miR-26b-5p for CASP4) in ASD. qRT-PCR in the VPA rat autism model confirmed increased TLR8 (hippocampus and blood) and CASP4 (hippocampus) expression, pointing to these as candidate ASD biomarkers and therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Comparative whole genome analysis of Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolated from BPaLM and individualized regimen treated patients at Dr. Soetomo Hospital, Indonesia.
papers.summary: Whole-genome sequencing of Mycobacterium tuberculosis from 14 rifampicin-resistant patients (8 BPaLM, 6 individualized regimens) at Dr. Soetomo Hospital, Indonesia, found Beijing lineage L2.2 predominant (48%). TBProfiler and Mykrobe showed higher sensitivity than ResFinder (86% vs 79%). Resistance mutations centered on rpoB, katG, embB, pncA; the BPaLM group showed a lower SNP burden, with no statistically significant between-group difference.

papers.title: Evolutionary co-option of endogenous retroviruses: syncytins as regulators of placental development and disease.
papers.summary: This review covers syncytin-1 (HERV-W) and syncytin-2 (HERV-FRD), retrovirus-derived envelope proteins co-opted to fuse cytotrophoblasts into syncytiotrophoblast for placental nutrient transport and maternal-fetal immune tolerance. Aberrant syncytin expression is linked to preeclampsia, intrauterine growth restriction, gestational diabetes, and trophoblastic disease; viral infections (CMV, SARS-CoV-2) may disrupt their regulation. Syncytins exemplify evolutionary viral domestication essential to human reproduction.

papers.title: Salidroside alleviates sepsis-associated acute lung injury through modulation of the ERK/FoxO3a signaling axis and improvement of impaired autophagic flux.
papers.summary: Salidroside was evaluated in LPS-treated RLE-6TN cells and a CLP rat sepsis model of acute lung injury. Network pharmacology suggested the ERK/FoxO3a axis; salidroside reduced inflammation, improved impaired autophagic flux (lower p62, more autolysosomes), decreased ERK phosphorylation, and increased nuclear FoxO3a. The ERK activator PMA partially reversed these effects. Salidroside protects against sepsis-associated ALI via ERK/FoxO3a modulation and autophagy restoration.

papers.title: Pan-genome analysis reveals the triangle mechanisms of antibiotic resistance, pathogenicity, and biofilm formation in Enterococcus faecalis.
papers.summary: Pan-genome analysis of 214 Enterococcus faecalis genomes identified 36 potential drug targets (15 non-enzymatic, 21 enzymatic, mostly cytoplasmic including four surface proteins). Resistance-conferring genes included ABC transporters, MFS proteins, and efflux pumps mediating resistance to glycopeptides, quinolones, aminoglycosides, and tetracyclines. Reveals the interconnected mechanisms of antibiotic resistance, pathogenicity, and biofilm formation in this nosocomial pathogen.

papers.title: SLC25A38 gene modification mediated by CRISPR/Cas9 in HEK293T cell line.
papers.summary: The authors designed six sgRNAs targeting SLC25A38 (linked to sideroblastic anemia) and built recombinant PX458/PX459 plasmids for transfection into HEK293T cells. PAGE-based analysis and Sanger sequencing confirmed the CRISPR/Cas9 system created targeted disruption at the desired site in three of four samples. sgRNA target-site choice affects cleavage activity, and spCas9 with guide RNA can delete an exonic fragment of SLC25A38.

papers.title: Protein Kinase C-delta (PKCδ) in Neurodegeneration and Cerebral Ischemia: Molecular Mechanisms and Therapeutic Implications.
papers.summary: This review examines PKCdelta (a calcium-independent novel PKC isoform) in Parkinson's, Alzheimer's, Huntington's disease, and ischemic stroke. It emphasizes cell-type- and disease-specific mechanisms: in PD it amplifies dopaminergic injury and glial inflammation; in AD it links amyloid processing, Abeta-induced stress, and neuroinflammation; in stroke it drives reperfusion oxidative/inflammatory injury. Isoform-selective, compartment- and cell-type-resolved modulation is proposed for therapy.

papers.title: Comparative Efficacy of Coriander Seed Extract-Loaded Selenium Nanoparticles and DMSA in Restoring Antioxidant/Apoptotic Balance of Lead-Induced Hepatotoxicity.
papers.summary: Coriander extract-loaded selenium nanoparticles (coriander@Se-NPs) were tested against lead-induced hepatotoxicity in mice versus the chelator DMSA. The nanoparticles reduced hepatic lead by 83.90%, restored SOD and catalase, showed a 12.5-fold reduction in IL-6, suppressed caspase-3, and stabilized beclin-1, outperforming DMSA on antioxidant/apoptotic balance. Presents coriander@Se-NPs as a multimodal nanomedicine against heavy-metal poisoning.

papers.title: Elucidation of Baicalein's Anti-Intervertebral Disc Degeneration Mechanism Through Network Pharmacology and Experimental Validation.
papers.summary: Network pharmacology and in vitro validation defined baicalein's effects on intervertebral disc degeneration in IL-1beta-treated nucleus pulposus cells. Baicalein (50 uM) promoted viability, inhibited apoptosis via Bcl-2/Bax and cleaved caspase-3, reduced TNF-alpha and IL-6, restored ECM homeostasis (MMP-3, aggrecan, collagen II), and suppressed ERK/p38 phosphorylation. The MAPK agonist anisomycin partially reversed these effects, indicating baicalein acts mainly through MAPK inhibition.

papers.title: Rosemary (Rosmarinus officinalis) Extract Attenuates Methotrexate-Induced Oxidative Stress, Inflammatory Disturbance, and Apoptotic Lung Injury: A Molecular and Histopathological Study.
papers.summary: In adult Wistar rats, methotrexate (MTX) increased ROS, MDA, TNF-alpha, p53 expression/immunoreactivity, and collagen, while decreasing GSH, IL-6, and Bcl-2. Co-treatment with Rosemary (Rosmarinus officinalis) extract attenuated these MTX-induced oxidative, inflammatory, and apoptotic changes in lung tissue and partially restored GSH and Bcl-2. Recovery was partial rather than complete; further mechanistic and translational studies are warranted.
